description: Main window: read/write the app-data workspace; native dialogs for import/export; clipboard for copy actions; shell to run Diogenes' perl exporter and pandoc as subprocesses. The fs:allow-exists scope covers onboarding's existence checks only (Diogenes install location and the user-picked TLG folder). The broader read/write/mkdir/read-dir/stat '/**' scopes support a user-picked library folder (shared-folder sync, build spec §11) — the folder is chosen explicitly via the native picker, same trust model as the TLG folder. The pandoc-homebrew/pandoc-usr-local entries pin ABSOLUTE pandoc paths: a Finder-launched .app inherits launchd's minimal PATH (no Homebrew dirs), so the bare 'pandoc' name only works from a terminal launch — the frontend probes which absolute path exists and prefers it (src/lib/export/pandoc.ts), keeping bare 'pandoc' as the last resort. The AI-assist commands (assist_which/assist_run — d7 §B, replacing the former Claude-specific assist_resolve_claude/assist_suggest) are app-owned Rust commands registered via invoke_handler (src-tauri/src/assist.rs) — they are not plugin commands, so they need no shell scope here; core:default covers app commands. Security boundary (d7 §B): assist_run executes a frontend-named ABSOLUTE executable with a frontend-supplied argv array; the binaries actually invoked come from the fixed built-in tool registry (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini) plus the user's explicit custom-command config — the same trust as the user running that tool in their own terminal. The prompt is data (a stdin stream or a single argv element under execve), never shell syntax, so no shell ever parses it. assist_which validates bin_name against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ before it is interpolated into the login-shell 'command -v' resolution rung, rejecting any shell metacharacter without running the shell. This is a small, documented widening of an app-owned command that previously only ran 'claude'. fs:allow-read-file is what the TLG/PHI importer needs and is NOT implied by fs:allow-read: 'read' is the byte-range command on an open handle, 'read_file' slurps a whole file, and AUTHTAB.DIR and the .IDT indexes are binary, so read-text-file cannot serve them. Its scope matches the read-text-file grant already present. The open/read/seek entries exist for Latin lookup: Diogenes' latin-analyses.txt is ~43MB and must be read by byte range through its companion index rather than slurped whole (src/lib/lexicon/latinAnalyses.ts), and the existing read-text-file/stat scopes are whole-file only. Their '/**' scope matches the read-text-file grant already present — the file being read is the user's own Diogenes install, whose location the user sets. run_program (src-tauri/src/assist.rs) is the assist_run sibling used to run a user-chosen pandoc for export: same trust boundary — an absolute executable picked by the user through the native file picker, run under execve with a frontend argv array — differing only in that it reports the exit code plainly instead of treating empty stdout as failure, which pandoc's silent success would otherwise trip. run_program also accepts an optional working directory and environment for the TLG/PHI corpus importer (src/lib/import/discImport.ts): Diogenes' xml-export.pl loads its own modules by relative path so it only runs from its own directory, and it locates the user's disc through TLG_DIR/PHI_DIR. Neither widens the boundary: the environment is restricted in Rust to a FIXED allow-list of those disc variables (ALLOWED_ENV in assist.rs), so PATH, PERL5LIB, DYLD_* and anything else that would change which code the interpreter loads are dropped with a log line rather than passed through; a working directory that is not an existing directory falls back to the neutral temp dir.
